meta_description: See Alberta speeding demerit bands, the court threshold, response options, official sources, and when a ticket-specific review may help.
h1: Alberta Speeding Tickets: Demerits, Court and Your Options
hook: An officer-issued Alberta speeding conviction carries two to six demerit points depending on the alleged speed, and speeding at 51 km/h or more over the limit requires a court appearance.
bullets: Two demerit points apply for speeding up to 15 km/h over the limit.
Three demerit points apply for speeding 16 to 30 km/h over the limit.
Four demerit points apply for speeding 31 to 50 km/h over the limit.
Six demerit points apply for speeding 51 km/h or more over the limit, with a mandatory court appearance.
what:
What an Alberta speeding conviction means

The current Alberta Driver's Guide lists four speeding bands: two demerit points up to 15 km/h over, three for 16 to 30 km/h over, four for 31 to 50 km/h over, and six for 51 km/h or more over. The highest band also requires a court appearance.

Demerit points are applied on the conviction date, not the ticket date. They remain on the driving record for two years from the conviction date. A full-licence suspension starts at 15 or more points in a two-year period; a GDL suspension starts at eight or more.
how:
How to respond

Start with the response instructions and deadline printed on the ticket. Alberta's Traffic Ticket Digital Service can be used to pay, ask for time to pay, plead not guilty, ask for a trial date, or ask for a prosecutor review where that action is available.

Before choosing a response, preserve the ticket and any relevant photographs, video, or documents. Request the available disclosure and compare the allegation with the officer notes, device records, location, signs, and circumstances.
next:
What to do next

The sensible response depends on the alleged speed, the evidence, the existing driving record, and the practical value of a different outcome. No service can predict the result of an individual matter.

Fabsy can review the ticket and explain whether the matter is eligible for agent representation. Fabsy is an agent service, not a law firm.

Representation uses a $488 base representation fee plus 30% of any fine reduction achieved; there is no success fee if the fine is not reduced.

faqs.q: How many demerits can an Alberta speeding ticket carry?
faqs.a: The current Alberta schedule ranges from two demerit points for speeding up to 15 km/h over the limit to six points for speeding 51 km/h or more over the limit.

faqs.q: When is court mandatory for an Alberta speeding ticket?
faqs.a: The current Alberta Driver's Guide states that speeding at 51 km/h or more over the limit requires a court appearance. Follow the instructions printed on the ticket.

faqs.q: When are demerit points added to my record?
faqs.a: Alberta applies demerit points on the conviction date, not the date the ticket was issued. Paying the ticket is one way a conviction date can be created.
